content.text: The docs already say "The port parsed from `request.host`" — the code had drifted from the documented behavior. Let me review the final diff:

Done. Not committed, as asked.

## The fix

`lib/request.js:259` — `port` now parses from `this.host` instead of re-reading `this.headers.host ?? this.headers[':authority']`:

```js
port: {
  get () {
    const portReg = /(?<port>:\d+)$/
    // Derived from `host` so that `host`, `hostname` and `port` always agree,
    // including when `host` comes from `x-forwarded-host` under trustProxy.
    const matches = portReg.exec(this.host)
```

The parsing logic from #6603 is untouched; only the source changed. This works for both constructor variants without duplicating anything: `port` and `hostname` live on `Request.prototype`, while the trust-proxy builder overrides `host` on the subclass prototype, so `this.host` dispatches to the trust-proxy getter when present. That's what keeps the plain and trust-proxy builders in step, per COMPLEX.md's instruction for this file.

One behavioral detail worth flagging: the plain `host` getter reads `this.raw.headers`, whereas `port` previously read `this.headers` (which merges `additionalHeaders` set via `request.headers = {...}`). After the fix `port` follows `host`, so a `host` injected through that setter no longer affects `port` — which is exactly how `hostname` already behaved, so the three are now consistent.

## Tests

- **`test/request-port.test.js`** — added trust-proxy coverage for #6671: `x-forwarded-host` with/without a port, multi-value headers (last entry wins), IPv6, `Host` fallback, **`:authority` fallback**, `x-forwarded-host` over `:authority`, no-host-at-all, and an untrusted-connection case. Each asserts `host`/`hostname`/`port` together so drift between them fails.
- **`test/trust-proxy.test.js`** — added an end-to-end alignment test, and corrected six existing tests whose expectations encoded the old behavior. They all send `x-forwarded-host: fastify.test` (no port) while asserting `port === app.server.address().port` — i.e. a `host` of `fastify.test` alongside a port from the `Host` header, precisely the disagreement this issue is about. Expected `port` is now `null`, the guard changed from truthy to `!== undefined` so `null` is actually asserted rather than skipped, and plan counts dropped accordingly.

I verified the new test is not vacuous by reverting the source change: it fails with `actual: 3000, expected: 8080`.

## Verification

`test/request-port.test.js`, `test/trust-proxy.test.js`, `test/request-header-host.test.js`, `test/internals/request.test.js`, `test/internals/reply.test.js`, `test/hostname-port.test.js` — 120 tests, all passing. I ran the reply internals alongside the request tests since COMPLEX.md notes the two move together; **`lib/reply.js` needed no change** — it doesn't read `port`.

Two things I could not do: **lint was blocked by the sandbox** (`npx eslint` and `npm run lint` both denied), so style is unverified by tooling, though the changes follow the surrounding `standard` style. I also did not run the full suite, only the covering tests for this area.

No docs change was needed — `docs/Reference/Request.md:31` already documents `port` as "The port parsed from `request.host`", so the code had drifted from the documented contract and now matches it again.

Done. Not committed, as asked.

## The fix

`lib/request.js:259` — `port` now parses from `this.host` instead of re-reading `this.headers.host ?? this.headers[':authority']`:

```js
port: {
  get () {
    const portReg = /(?<port>:\d+)$/
    // Derived from `host` so that `host`, `hostname` and `port` always agree,
    // including when `host` comes from `x-forwarded-host` under trustProxy.
    const matches = portReg.exec(this.host)
```

The parsing logic from #6603 is untouched; only the source changed. This works for both constructor variants without duplicating anything: `port` and `hostname` live on `Request.prototype`, while the trust-proxy builder overrides `host` on the subclass prototype, so `this.host` dispatches to the trust-proxy getter when present. That's what keeps the plain and trust-proxy builders in step, per COMPLEX.md's instruction for this file.

One behavioral detail worth flagging: the plain `host` getter reads `this.raw.headers`, whereas `port` previously read `this.headers` (which merges `additionalHeaders` set via `request.headers = {...}`). After the fix `port` follows `host`, so a `host` injected through that setter no longer affects `port` — which is exactly how `hostname` already behaved, so the three are now consistent.

## Tests

- **`test/request-port.test.js`** — added trust-proxy coverage for #6671: `x-forwarded-host` with/without a port, multi-value headers (last entry wins), IPv6, `Host` fallback, **`:authority` fallback**, `x-forwarded-host` over `:authority`, no-host-at-all, and an untrusted-connection case. Each asserts `host`/`hostname`/`port` together so drift between them fails.
- **`test/trust-proxy.test.js`** — added an end-to-end alignment test, and corrected six existing tests whose expectations encoded the old behavior. They all send `x-forwarded-host: fastify.test` (no port) while asserting `port === app.server.address().port` — i.e. a `host` of `fastify.test` alongside a port from the `Host` header, precisely the disagreement this issue is about. Expected `port` is now `null`, the guard changed from truthy to `!== undefined` so `null` is actually asserted rather than skipped, and plan counts dropped accordingly.

I verified the new test is not vacuous by reverting the source change: it fails with `actual: 3000, expected: 8080`.

## Verification

`test/request-port.test.js`, `test/trust-proxy.test.js`, `test/request-header-host.test.js`, `test/internals/request.test.js`, `test/internals/reply.test.js`, `test/hostname-port.test.js` — 120 tests, all passing. I ran the reply internals alongside the request tests since COMPLEX.md notes the two move together; **`lib/reply.js` needed no change** — it doesn't read `port`.

Two things I could not do: **lint was blocked by the sandbox** (`npx eslint` and `npm run lint` both denied), so style is unverified by tooling, though the changes follow the surrounding `standard` style. I also did not run the full suite, only the covering tests for this area.

No docs change was needed — `docs/Reference/Request.md:31` already documents `port` as "The port parsed from `request.host`", so the code had drifted from the documented contract and now matches it again.
